total_return_swap_trs.text: `swaption_pricer_black` prices a European option on a swap rate, while `total_return_swap_trs` values one leg of a total-return swap. The swaption function answers "what is the right to enter a swap at a given strike worth today?" It takes `forward_swap_rate`, `strike`, `vol`, `expiry` and `annuity`, and treats a payer swaption as a call on the swap rate and a receiver as a put. The total-return swap function answers "what is the leg worth, given the asset's return against a financing rate?" It takes `asset_return`, `financing_rate`, `accrual` and `discount_factor`, and has no volatility or optionality. In short, one prices an option whose value depends on rate volatility, and the other values a swap leg from the asset return, the financing cost and discounting.

explain.text: `swaption_pricer_black` (Swaption Pricer Black) prices a European swaption under the Black model. It takes the `notional`, `forward_swap_rate`, `strike`, `vol`, `expiry` and `annuity`, and returns the price as the annuity times a Black formula value, scaled by notional. A payer swaption is treated as a call on the swap rate, and a receiver swaption as a put. You choose between them with `option_type`, which defaults to `"payer"`. The `annuity` input is the present value of a 1-unit fixed annuity (level / PVBP), and the rates are entered as decimals.

when.text:
`swaption_pricer_black` (Swaption Pricer Black) fits when you need the price of a European swaption under the Black model.

- You have a single European swaption, a payer (a call on the swap rate) or a receiver (a put), and want its value from `notional`, `forward_swap_rate`, `strike`, `vol`, `expiry` and `annuity`.
- You can quote a single Black volatility for the swap rate and are happy to treat it as flat across the calculation.
- You already have the annuity (the PV of a 1-unit fixed annuity, also called PVBP) from your curve and just need the option value on top of it.
- You want a quick, standard lognormal benchmark for a swaption quote.

If you'd rather have the volatility come from a smile model, `swaption_pricer_sabr` is listed as pricing a swaption using a SABR-implied Black volatility.
